panels.title: Write Claims Declined (backend full)
panels.description: Writes a backend refused for want of room. The headroom test is the insert that claims the space, against live rows, so this is the authoritative signal that a backend is full - not an in-memory estimate. A write declined here moved to the next candidate; when every candidate declines, the request fails with 507. Sustained non-zero on one backend means it needs capacity or a drain.

panels.title: Quota Drift Corrections
panels.description: Byte-total corrections applied by usage reconciliation. The counter now moves inside the same transaction that writes the object rows it summarizes, so it cannot drift from the ledger: this is expected to stay at zero for the life of the process. Any increase means a mutation path is storing bytes without charging them, and the reconcile is papering over it - investigate rather than ignore.

panels.title: Handler Panics Recovered
panels.description: A handler panicked and the recovery middleware returned 500. Any non-zero value is an alert; pivot via the matching http.PanicRecovered audit entry.

panels.title: Copies Placed by the Write
panels.description: Further copies a write placed itself rather than leaving to the replicator, by what became of each. committed is the copy landing and being recorded. untrusted is a newer write taking the key while the copy was still uploading, so it was discarded and replication rebuilds it - each one costs a rebuild. failed is the backend refusing it. Zero across all three with the fan-out on means no write is placing extra copies at all.

panels.title: Copies Committed per Write
panels.description: Mean copies a fan-out write ended up committing, counting the one that answered the client. This is the number that says whether the feature is working: sitting at replication.factor means writes reach it unaided, and drifting toward 1 means they are degrading to a single copy while the replicator quietly picks the difference back up. The panels either side say why.

panels.title: Detached Uploads In Flight
panels.description: Writes whose further copies are still uploading after their client was answered. A healthy fleet sits at roughly the write rate times how long one copy takes - a handful. A rising floor is the signal a backend is slow rather than broken: nothing fails and nothing retries, the work just accumulates until the ceiling (write_path.parallel_copies.max_in_flight) turns the fan-out off.

panels.title: Fan-Out Skipped (no slot)
panels.description: Writes that placed a single copy because the in-flight ceiling was full, leaving the rest to the replicator. Every one costs exactly what the fan-out exists to avoid - a read of the object plus the source backend's egress - so a sustained rate means either max_in_flight is too low for the write rate or a backend is falling behind. The depth panel to the left says which.

panels.title: Request Pool Usage (% of limit)
panels.description: Per-pool share of the monthly request budget. Providers meter operations in classes with separate allowances, so this is the figure a backend is refused on - Monthly API Requests counts every call, including ones no budget charges. Unlimited pools are omitted.

panels.title: CORS Preflights
panels.description: Browser preflights by outcome. Rejections climbing with no allowed series means the bucket's CORS rules do not cover the origin the application is served from, and every browser upload from it is failing.

panels.title: Encryption Flag Mismatches
panels.description: An object's stored bytes disagree with its recorded encryption flag, so that copy cannot be read or hashed. Any non-zero value is an alert.

panels.title: Verification Coverage (oldest unverified)
panels.description: How long ago the least recently verified copy was checked. Should sit flat around the period implied by scrubber_interval and scrubber_batch_size; a steadily climbing line means the sweep cannot keep pace with the fleet.

panels.title: Copies Never Verified
panels.description: Copies with a content hash the scrubber has not reached yet. Stays non-zero on a fleet being written to, since new copies queue behind older data by design. Alert on a climbing value, not on it being above zero.

panels.title: Unreadable Imports
panels.description: Reconcile or sync found an encrypted object whose key is gone. Unrecoverable: restore from elsewhere or delete it. Any non-zero rate wants a human.

panels.title: Pending Intents Depth
panels.description: Unresolved PUT intents. An intent holds its bytes against the backend's headroom for as long as it lives, so a stuck one is space no write can use, not just a commit awaiting repair. Steady-state should be 0; persistent non-zero indicates the reaper is not draining (DB outage, backend HEAD failures, or operator-review-required ambiguous rows).

panels.title: Pending Intent Throughput
panels.description: Rate of intents enqueued by the write path versus resolved by status. Steady state has enqueued and committed close to equal; promoted/dropped events indicate the reaper is repairing failed commits.

panels.title: Ambiguous Intents (lifetime)
panels.description: Lifetime count of pending intents the reaper refused to promote because the destination already held a row for the same key. These rows stay in the database for operator review; any non-zero value warrants investigation.

panels.title: Streaming Payload Requests
panels.description: Rate of streaming-SigV4 PUTs received, by AWS streaming variant.

panels.title: Streaming Payload Rejections
panels.description: Rate of streaming-SigV4 PUTs rejected mid-stream, by reason. Any non-zero rate is either a misconfigured client or a tampered request.

panels.title: Worker tick rate by service & result
Rows graduated to DLQ by backend
Degraded mode active
panels.description: 1 when the DB circuit breaker is open or half-open; reads broadcast across backends.

panels.title: Degraded broadcast duration
panels.description: Wall-clock p50/p95/p99 of degraded-mode broadcast reads, by terminal outcome.

panels.title: Degraded broadcast mixed outcomes
panels.description: Rate of broadcasts where backends disagreed: some returned 404 while others failed with non-404 errors. Persistent non-zero values suggest provider divergence or a transient backend storm hidden under not_found.

panels.title: Broadcast Drain Timeouts
panels.description: Loser-drain goroutines that gave up at the bounded timeout because a cancelled probe never returned. Non-zero means a backend is stranding goroutines under degraded fan-out.
